clue.text: Necklace material about right for a pound

indicators.note: the necklace material is wrapped about the letter for right, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: coral is a material often strung into necklaces

explanation.surface: A jeweller weighs up whether the right necklace material is worth a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money or weight, but here it is an enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is an enclosure for stray animals, and a pen for livestock is the same thing, a synonym.

clue.text: A bicycle breaking down — and avoiding it

indicators.note: a bicycle breaking down falls to pieces, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A cyclist's machine falls apart, and they decide to give up riding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the old euphemism for sex, so 'avoiding it' is a coy definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from sex is the meaning of the answer, with 'it' standing in coyly for sexual activity.

clue.text: Raced extremely gamely, having long legs

parts.note: raced means ran

indicators.note: extremely takes only the extreme letters of the word gamely, its first and last

explanation.surface: A long-legged runner sprinted with great pluck to the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangy describes a person or animal that is tall and slim with long limbs.

clue.text: The sound of a sneeze subject to dispute

indicators.note: the clue asks for how the noise of a sneeze is heard, so a word that resembles it when spoken

parts.note: atishoo is the British written form of a sneeze, like achoo

explanation.surface: Someone sneezes noisily, and nobody can agree what it means.
explanation.walkthrough: ATISHOO is the British spelling of a sneeze (American 'achoo'); said aloud it is close to AT ISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that is under debate or contention is said to be the point in question, an idiom.

clue.text: Blunder by Republican boss

parts.note: a blunder is a gaffe

explanation.surface: A Republican leader makes an embarrassing slip.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFFER is British informal for a boss or foreman.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the person in charge of a workplace or team is called the gaffer, a synonym.

clue.text: Continent brings slight change to a Saxon kingdom

indicators.note: a small rearrangement is made to the letters of the words before, so they are shuffled

parts.note: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A whole landmass is produced by tweaking an old English realm.
explanation.walkthrough: A is kept as it is; only two letters of MERCIA swap places, hence 'slight change'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Americas, North and South, form a landmass often counted as a single continent.

clue.text: Stupid old man almost dead unfortunately

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite finished, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: old man is informal for father

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go wrong, so the letters of dead are jumbled

explanation.surface: A foolish father has sadly almost died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims FATHER to FATHE; 'unfortunately' rearranges DEAD to ADED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thick-headed and foolish is called fat-headed, an informal synonym for dim.

clue.text: Pretty, that woman coming after despicable chap

indicators.note: the woman's word comes after the chap's word, setting their order

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person
her is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: A woman shows up after some contemptible man has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' is an adverb here, as in 'pretty good', not an adjective for good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: As adverbs meaning fairly or somewhat, the two are synonyms: pretty cold, rather cold.

clue.text: Give flattery that's rather mild apparently

parts.note: mild means bland
the suffix -ish means rather or somewhat, as in reddish

explanation.surface: Flattery that is a little lukewarm seems to do the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as BLAND-ISH, 'rather mild'; 'apparently' signals the jokey reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To blandish is to coax someone with flattering words, a verb meaning to cajole.

clue.text: Wessex writer to cancel penning a regular feature

parts.note: Thomas Hardy set his novels in a fictional Wessex

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to cancel is to annul

explanation.surface: A novelist is asked to scrap a regular column he writes.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy's novels are set in 'Wessex', his name for south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recurring every year, like a festival or story, is called a hardy annual, an idiom from gardening.

clue.text: Large car is in France and corroded

parts.note: est is French for is
corroded means ate away

explanation.surface: A big vehicle is in France and has gone rusty.
explanation.walkthrough: An ESTATE is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a big car with a rear load area and tailgate is an estate, an American station wagon.

clue.text: Follow order how to address Turkish governor?

parts.note: O is the vocative used to address someone, as in O king
a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A courtier asks the proper way to greet an Ottoman official.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply with a command, or follow an order, is to do as told.

clue.text: Reinstated imbecile in distress

indicators.note: imbecile treats the word reinstated as foolishly muddled, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A foolish worker gets their job back and is still in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Straitened circumstances are poverty or hardship, so the word means suffering need.

clue.text: Menial worker could be a clumsy idler

indicators.note: the words could be rearranged into something else, so their letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A lowly servant might turn out to be an awkward layabout.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullery maid was the lowest servant in a big house, washing dishes in the back kitchen.

clue.text: Girl holding banal procedure before the end

indicators.note: the girl holds the other word, so it sits inside her

parts.note: lass is a girl
banal means trite

explanation.surface: A young woman is stuck with a dull routine until the job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: The final sacraments given to a dying person are a ceremony performed before death.

clue.text: Girl who's marrying one of the Guards welcomes soldier in Spanish resort

indicators.note: the girl welcomes the soldier in, taking him inside her name

parts.words: Girl who's marrying one of the Guards
parts.note: in A. A. Milne's poem about Buckingham Palace, Alice is marrying one of the guard
a soldier ant, so ant

explanation.surface: A soldier's bride greets another soldier at a Spanish holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl comes from A. A. Milne's poem 'Buckingham Palace': 'Alice is marrying one of the guard'. A soldier is an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a port and beach town on Spain's Costa Blanca, an example of a resort.

clue.text: Subordinate to support scam

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
a fiddle is a swindle

explanation.surface: A junior employee is asked to back a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing second fiddle means taking a lesser role, so the phrase names someone in a lower position.

clue.text: Continue to complain

definitions.meaning: to make a fuss or grumble, as in 'stop carrying on'

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on whingeing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to proceed and, informally, to make a noisy fuss.

clue.text: Transport French crew

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A French team moves goods about.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried by lorry, ship or train, or the act of carrying them.

clue.text: Warble about husband giving feeling of excitement

indicators.note: the warble goes about the husband's letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to warble is to trill

explanation.surface: A singer's warbling about her husband stirs her.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrill is a sudden surge of pleasure or excitement, a synonym.

clue.text: Liqueur to consume again put on table perhaps

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece put on another comes after it

parts.note: a table of figures is one kind of chart
to reuse is to use again

explanation.surface: Someone sets a drink on the table so they can drink it again later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on table' reads like serving a drink, but CHART is the 'table perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a green or yellow French herbal spirit made by Carthusian monks.

clue.text: After last month, shortened king's platform

indicators.note: the king's letter comes after the shortened month
the month's name is cut short, leaving its usual abbreviation

parts.note: the last month of the year is December
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A king stands on a platform once December is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' cuts DECEMBER to DEC, its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A deck is a floor or raised surface, as on a ship or a patio, a synonym.

clue.text: Get out of army march with first touch of biliousness

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: only the first letter of biliousness is touched on

explanation.surface: A queasy soldier marches out of the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To demob is to discharge someone from military service, short for demobilise.

clue.text: Succeed in rugby move — biting!

parts.note: to succeed is to win
a try is the rugby score made by grounding the ball

explanation.surface: A rugby player scores by sinking their teeth in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting' looks like a verb about teeth; it means bitterly cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting weather is sharply cold, like winter, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: What footballer may damage in match — put dressing around it

indicators.note: the dressing goes around the match, enclosing it

parts.note: lint is a fabric used for dressing wounds
a match is a game

explanation.surface: A footballer injured in a match has a bandage wrapped round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is the tough tissue joining bones, often torn in a knee injury on the pitch.

clue.text: Down South I ache going around

indicators.note: the yearning word goes around the others, enclosing them

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Feeling low in the south, someone has pains all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like sad or a direction, but it means behind in a game, as in 'two goals down'.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that is down in a match is trailing on the scoreboard, a synonym.

clue.text: Secure accommodation for Arabs

definitions.meaning: firm and steady, not likely to give way
Arabs here are Arab horses, and a building where horses are kept

explanation.surface: A safe place to house Arab horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both firmly fixed and a building where horses are housed.
